```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 88)
library(readNBS)
```

Identify each NBS value with its reporting window, source vintage, release URL,
retrieval or archive hash, and classification or aggregation boundary.
`readNBS` keeps those fields explicit so analyses preserve source geometry
across releases and incompatible source tables remain distinct.

## Read the manifest behind a scalar ID

`nbs_manifest()` is local metadata. Its rows map a supported semantic ID to a
time-bounded transport slice and record the source contract used by the
parser:

```{r manifest}
manifest <- nbs_manifest()
cpi_slices <- manifest[
  manifest$series_id == "NBS/CN/M/CPI/HEADLINE/YOY_INDEX",
  c(
    "series_id", "slice_start", "slice_end", "classification_id",
    "period_policy", "aggregation_basis", "source_url", "source_note"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]
cpi_slices
```

The stable `series_id` is the supported user identity. The manifest maps
transport UUIDs to stable semantic IDs and validates coverage changes.

## Preserve source dates and vintages

This retained property release series is an entirely local example. The
transport guard ensures that the selected 2020 range is read from the
bundled first-release archive:

```{r retained-observations}
property_id <- "NBS/CN/M/PROPERTY_DEVELOPMENT/NATIONAL"
property_filters <- list(
  series_id = "NBS/CN/M/PROPERTY/FUNDING/DEPOSITS_ADVANCE_RECEIPTS/YTD_LEVEL"
)
offline <- nbs_client(
  transport = function(...) stop("The retained archive attempted a network request."),
  retries = 0L
)

property <- nbs_fetch_dataset(
  property_id,
  filters = property_filters,
  start = "2020-02",
  end = "2020-04",
  client = offline
)

property[c(
  "series_id", "period", "value", "unit", "reference_period_start",
  "reference_period_end", "aggregation_basis", "period_policy",
  "release_date", "vintage_date", "source_vintage", "source_url",
  "raw_sha256"
)]
```

Here `period` identifies the reported observation, while
`reference_period_start` and `reference_period_end` show that the February
observation covers January--February. `release_date` and `vintage_date`
describe the source, while `retrieved_at` records the package read and is `NA`
for this retained local read. Keep the source unit of 100 million yuan explicit
before applying a monthly-flow transformation.

## Make the reporting calendar explicit

For additive year-to-date levels, `nbs_regularise_monthly()` is an opt-in
analytical benchmark. It assigns half of the combined January--February value
to each month by default and differences subsequent cumulative observations.
The result is labelled as derived and retains the source periods and hashes:

```{r regularise}
monthly <- nbs_regularise_monthly(property)
monthly[c(
  "series_id", "period", "value", "unit", "derived_method",
  "source_observation_periods", "source_omitted_observation_periods",
  "source_vintage", "route"
)]
```

The January and February values are labelled derived accounting benchmarks and
remain distinct from official monthly observations. Use `working_day_share`
only with an independently verified calendar supplied through `working_days`;
rates, indexes, stocks, and incomplete cumulative series remain outside this
transformation.

## Convert a comparison index explicitly

NBS often publishes comparisons as an index with a base of 100. For a
same-month-previous-year index, the year-on-year percentage change is exactly
the index minus 100. The following uses the installed response snapshot, so
it remains offline while exercising the same parser used for a portal call:

```{r comparison-index}
fixture_path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "examples", "cpi-2026-june.json", package = "readNBS"
)
fixture_body <- paste(
  readLines(fixture_path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"),
  collapse = "\n"
)
fixture_transport <- function(request) {
  list(
    status = 200L,
    headers = list(`content-type` = "application/json"),
    body = fixture_body
  )
}
fixture_client <- nbs_client(
  transport = fixture_transport,
  retries = 0L,
  now = function() as.POSIXct("2026-07-29 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
cpi <- nbs_fetch_series(
  "NBS/CN/M/CPI/HEADLINE/YOY_INDEX",
  start = "2026-06",
  end = "2026-06",
  client = fixture_client
)
comparison <- nbs_comparison_index_to_percent(cpi)
comparison[c(
  "period", "value", "source_index_value", "raw_value", "unit",
  "derived_method", "source_raw_sha256"
)]
```

The input is unchanged, the original index remains in `source_index_value`
and `raw_value`, and the derived method is recorded. This helper records the
index-minus-100 identity; seasonal adjustment and rebasing remain separate
workflows.

## Keep provenance in downstream files

For a report or model input, save at least:

* the stable `series_id` or `dataset_id` and canonical `dimension_key`;
* requested and returned `period` values plus the reference-period fields;
* `source_vintage`, `data_status`, release and vintage dates;
* `source_url`, `source_note`, `raw_sha256`, and `source_raw_sha256`; and
* `manifest_version`, `parser_version`, `package_version`, and any
  `derived_method`.

Retained press and Yearbook rows preserve a labelled release vintage. Portal
rows describe the latest/revised database state returned at fetch time. These
are different source contracts even when their titles look similar. NBS
classification, base-period, and coverage breaks remain visible in the
`series_note` fields. Combine eras only through an explicit, documented
mapping.

For a practical way to inspect an exact panel selector before choosing its
source, see [Selecting dimensional NBS datasets](dimensional-datasets.html).
